subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer packaging & channel split
messages:
From: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer — packaging + channel pass-through question

Thanks for the demo today, Irene — product looks promising. We want to move to procurement, but two things came up on our side that we need clarity on before I can get the PO approved:

1) Packaging: Acme prefers a single private-offer SKU that bundles inference + support. Does Redwood support a single SKU on AWS private offer that maps to multiple underlying meter lines (tokens + hosting)? We need to avoid managing two separate line items in our ERP.

2) Channel split / reseller margin: Our reseller (CloudBridge) needs a standard 18% pass-through on list price. If we accept a private offer with a net price to Acme, can CloudBridge still invoice and receive their 18% from AWS, or do we need to structure a separate commission flow?

Can you point me to an example term sheet or explain typical flows? Appreciate any quick notes — procurement is on a tight cycle.

-Mark

[attachment: acme-ma-pricing-proposal.pdf (PDF)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — packaging + channel pass-through question

Mark — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a suggested next step: 

1) Packaging: Yes — on AWS Marketplace we can create a single private-offer SKU that represents a bundled product. The private offer can reference multiple internal meters (e.g., token consumption + reserved capacity) while presenting one consolidated line item to the buyer. In practice, we bind the meters in the private-offer configuration and provide a term sheet that shows the mapping for accounting.

2) Channel/reseller: There are two common patterns we see: 
  - List-price-based pass-through: the reseller invoices off the published list price; the private offer is structured so the reseller still receives their pass-through commission percentage from AWS. This usually requires the private offer to leave list price visible to the channel and use a separate discount bridge.
  - Net-price routing: the buyer pays net to Redwood via the private offer and the reseller is compensated directly by Redwood via a reseller agreement (out-of-band).

Which path fits Acme depends on your reseller contract. If CloudBridge requires standard AWS pass-through mechanics, we can coordinate with them and AWS Marketplace ops — it typically adds 3–5 business days and a short Ops form. If you prefer to keep the channel settlement off-market (so Redwood issues the reseller payment), we can do that too but it will be reflected as a line on Redwood invoices rather than AWS invoices.

Suggested next step: loop in CloudBridge billing contact and our Marketplace ops (Ben) for a quick alignment call. I attached a draft term-sheet that shows the SKU mapping.

Irene

--
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: private-offer-term-sheet.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: AWS private offer — packaging + channel pass-through question

Forwarding Acme's questions — adding notes on operational impact.

=== Ben's internal notes ===
Irene / Laura, quick ops checklist and risks: 
- Single SKU: trivial on our side; we'll need to map token meter ID + reserved instance meter IDs in the PO. Make sure finance has SKU mapping doc for their ERP.
- Pass-through: If CloudBridge wants to take commission from AWS list price, we must NOT use an off-market reseller payout. That demands the private offer keep list-price public and attach a partner pass-through configuration. AWS Marketplace ops requires partner acceptance (1–3 days) + verification of reseller registration.
- Tax & invoicing: List-price pass-through means the invoice will show AWS flows; if Redwood pays reseller, Redwood's invoice will show a separate commission line (impacts revenue recognition slightly differently).
- Overage credits: Acme asked about burst usage. We should propose a simple overage credit policy (e.g., 10% buffer) to avoid invoice disputes.

I'll join the alignment call and prepare the Marketplace ops checklist. Laura — can you draft the quick reseller agreement language (one paragraph) for the out-of-band option if needed?

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS private offer — packaging + channel pass-through question

Ben — will do. Draft language below (one-paragraph reseller settlement model) for internal review, then we can share with Acme/CloudBridge if they want the out-of-band flow: 

"Reseller settlement: Redwood will invoice Buyer (Acme Health) at the agreed net private-offer price. Redwood will separately remit an agreed reseller commission to CloudBridge per the reseller agreement. That commission will be paid within 30 days of Redwood invoicing the Buyer. Buyer acknowledges that reseller commission is handled off-AWS and does not affect the private-offer price or billing on AWS Marketplace."

Aditya — quick question for pricing: If we go list-price pass-through and maintain published list for commission calculation, what's the smallest incremental discount we can offer Acme while preserving an 18% pass-through to the reseller? We need to model the math for their procurement team. I can run the boilerplate once I have the off-list discount margin tolerance.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace pass-through math

Laura / team — rough numbers below (high level):
- Published list price (L): $100k/year (example bundle)
- CloudBridge pass-through: 18% of L = $18k
- If we want Redwood net effective revenue to be N, then discount D = L - N - reseller_commission_if_paid_by_aws (depends on who pays)

Pattern A (reseller paid from AWS list): Acme pays L on AWS, AWS pays CloudBridge $18k, Redwood receives (L - AWS fees - any pass-through). If we want Redwood to receive $70k net, then list has to be set so the 18% doesn't push Redwood below target.

Pattern B (Redwood pays reseller): Set private offer net to Acme = $82k (if we want to show lower invoice to buyer). Redwood then pays CloudBridge $14.76k (18% of a published list price we define) — mechanics get fiddly. In practice we model three columns: buyer-facing price, published list, and Redwood net. 

I'll prepare a small spreadsheet with a few scenarios (attached) and bring it to the call. Note: AWS fees and tax effects matter; I'll include conservative AWS transaction fees.

-Aditya

- We want a 10% overage buffer described in the term-sheet to reduce monthly disputes.

Irene / Ben — can you coordinate with CloudBridge billing (cc'd) and finalize the private-offer draft this week? Procurement needs the term sheet to sign off.

-Mark
